lesson.intro: Es el 'llevo… haciendo algo' del español. Se usa para actividades que empezaron en el pasado y siguen, o que acaban de terminar y se notan.
when: Duración de una actividad que sigue ahora, con for, since o How long (I've been studying English for two years).
Actividad reciente cuyo efecto se ve ahora (You're out of breath. — I've been running).
Simple frente a continuo: el simple cuenta resultados o cantidades (I've written three emails); el continuo destaca la actividad y su duración (I've been writing emails all morning).
Los verbos de estado (know, like, believe, belong, have = poseer) van en present perfect simple: I've known her for years.

form.label: Estructura
items: I've been waiting / She's been waiting
Negativa: I haven't been sleeping well
Pregunta: How long have you been waiting?

examples.en: I've been studying English for two years.
It has been raining all day.
Why are you so tired? — I've been working in the garden.
examples.es: ¿Por qué estás tan cansado? — He estado trabajando en el jardín.

examples.en: She has read three books this month.
examples.es: Ha leído tres libros este mes (cantidad: simple).

errors.wrong: I'm waiting here for an hour.
errors.right: I've been waiting here for an hour.
errors.why: 'Llevo una hora esperando' no va en presente continuo, sino en present perfect continuous.

errors.wrong: I've been knowing him for years.
errors.why: 'Know' es de estado: present perfect simple.

errors.wrong: I have been written three emails.
errors.why: Con una cantidad (three emails) se usa el simple, y 'been written' sería pasiva.

lesson.tip: Si en español dirías 'llevo X tiempo haciendo…', en inglés casi siempre es have been + -ing.

checks.prompt: I ___ for you for twenty minutes!
checks.explain: 'Llevo veinte minutos esperando': have been waiting.

checks.prompt: She ___ four cups of coffee today.
checks.explain: Cantidad concreta (four cups): present perfect simple.

practice.prompt: You look frozen! How long ___ here?
practice.explain: Duración hasta ahora con How long: have you been standing.
Empezó esta mañana y sigue: has been raining.
Número concreto de cosas terminadas: present perfect simple.

practice.prompt: Your eyes are red. Have you ___ (cry)?
practice.explain: Actividad reciente con efecto visible: have you been crying.

answers: I have been studying English since 2020.
practice.explain: 'Desde 2020' y sigue: present perfect (mejor continuo para la actividad).

practice.sentence: We have been knowing each other for ten years.
answers: We have known each other for ten years.
I've been waiting for you for two hours.
I've been waiting for you for 2 hours.
practice.explain: 'Llevo + tiempo + gerundio' = have been + -ing + for + tiempo.

practice.prompt: She's tired because she ___ all afternoon.
practice.explain: Actividad larga que explica cómo está ahora: has been playing.

practice.prompt: Hemos estado viviendo aquí desde enero.
answers: We've been living here since January.
We have lived here since January.
practice.explain: Desde enero y sigue: have been living (o have lived).

challenge.sentence: I started learning the guitar two years ago and I'm still learning.
challenge.explain: Empezó hace dos años y sigue: have been + -ing.

challenge.sentence: It started snowing at 6 o'clock and it's still snowing.
challenge.explain: Punto de inicio con since + present perfect continuous.

challenge.prompt: I ___ this book for weeks, but I still haven't finished it.
challenge.explain: Actividad no terminada con duración: have been reading.

answers: How long have you been waiting?
challenge.explain: How long + actividad hasta ahora: have you been waiting.

challenge.es: Ha estado lloviendo toda la mañana.
challenge.explain: Actividad continua hasta ahora: has been raining.
